questions.q: According to the summary, why did Delhi's planners build a road they knew would be too small?
a: Indian culture frowned on excess and expected shortages
They lacked the money to build it any larger
They expected traffic to fall in future years
Foreign engineers designed it incorrectly
questions.why: Lesson 1 links the undersized road to a cultural belief that bigger, complex things waste time and resources.

questions.q: How does an Indian truck driver spend most of his working time, per the summary?
a: Only about 40 percent is spent actually driving
Nearly all of it is spent on open highways
Half is spent loading and unloading goods
Most of it is spent sleeping at checkpoints
questions.why: Lesson 1 says roughly 60 percent of a driver's time goes to traffic and tax checkpoint queues rather than driving.

questions.q: Why are factory jobs so scarce in India, according to the summary?
a: Regulations make it nearly impossible to fire workers
There are not enough workers to fill them
Factories are moving back to agriculture
The government owns almost every factory
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that employers keep staff small because rules make replacing unproductive workers very hard.

questions.q: What is true of Indian farming in the summary?
a: Farms are shrinking and wages are too low to attract workers
Farmland has doubled since 1970
Farming accounts for most of India's GDP
Farmers earn more than factory workers
questions.why: Lesson 2 notes that available farmland is half of what it was in 1970 and that farming pays too little to draw people in.

questions.q: What does the author call the main problem with letting private companies run projects?
a: They have too much power and no real oversight
They refuse to build any roads at all
They charge workers for using the roads
They always finish projects ahead of schedule
questions.why: Lesson 3 concludes that the central issue to fix is the excessive power held by the private sector.
